name: GLB improvement 1: assembly metric, repair retry, best-of-N, phase 2 data
description: Offline tooling for docs/14-glb-improvement.md. Measure whether an exported asset's parts actually fit together (the main reason Glimmer's assets are crude), add a one-shot repair retry and a best-of-N picker as product features, and build the phase 2 training set from ccore's validated dataset with an eval-leak guard. The owner then runs ralph/imp-ops.prd.json on this Mac and decides on the rented-GPU LoRA (docs/14 section 8).

userStories.title: Assembly metric: world-space part boxes, components, floaters (glb_check.mjs)
userStories.description: As the evaluator, I want an automatic measure of whether an asset's parts fit together, because scattered and floating parts are the main reason Glimmer's assets look crude (docs/14 sections 2 and 4).
steps: Extend tests/js/glb_util.mjs makeGlb with an optional `nodes` array: each entry {mesh: index, translation?, rotation?, scale?, matrix?, children?} plus `scene` (root node indices). Positions per mesh come from a `boxes` option [{min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]}] so tests can place unit boxes anywhere. Existing makeGlb calls must produce identical bytes.

In scripts/glb_check.mjs export `assembly(json, {kind = 'static', tolFrac = 0.02} = {})` implementing docs/14 section 4 exactly: world matrices from matrix or TRS (quaternion rotation), 8-corner transform of each POSITION min/max, union box, tol = tolFrac * union diagonal, touch graph, components, largest_share, floaters, min_y, ground_gap, assembled (kind-aware). Return {parts, components, largest_share, floaters, min_y, ground_gap, tol, assembled}. Never throw: on malformed input return {parts: 0, assembled: false, error: '<short reason>'}.
Have parseGlb include `assembly` (computed with kind 'static') in its result when ok, without changing any existing field.

Create tests/js/glb_assembly.test.mjs (imported from tests/js/index.js) covering: two touching boxes -> 1 component, assembled; two boxes 1 m apart in x on the ground -> 2 components, largest_share 0.5, not assembled for kind static but assembled for kind set; a box lifted 0.5 m off the ground and touching nothing -> 1 floater; a box resting on another box -> not a floater; a child node translated by its parent (hierarchy applied); a node with a 90 degree quaternion rotation; a node using `matrix`; malformed json -> no throw.
acceptanceCriteria: assembly() returns the exact components, largest_share, floaters and assembled values asserted for each of the 8 cases above
Existing glb_check tests still pass unchanged and makeGlb without the new options yields byte-identical output (asserted against a buffer built before the change or a stored hash)
parseGlb results gain an `assembly` object and keep every previous field with the same values
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Validator stores assembly; backfill CLI for existing runs (glb_assembly.mjs)
userStories.description: As the evaluator, I want assembly recorded for every new GLB-mode run and computed for runs already on disk, so v2, v3 and ccore can be compared without regenerating anything.
steps: In scripts/validate_scenes.mjs GLB mode, look up each brief's `kind` from the raw row (row.brief.kind) or from a new optional `--briefs FILE` flag, and store `stats.glb.assembly` = assembly(json, {kind}). Do not add or change any failure reason; scene mode is untouched.

Create scripts/glb_assembly.mjs CLI: `node scripts/glb_assembly.mjs --run RUN_DIR --briefs bench/glb/briefs.jsonl [--tol-frac 0.02]`. For each id in RUN_DIR/validation.jsonl with ok true, read the GLB the validator wrote under RUN_DIR/glb/ (find the naming in validate_scenes.mjs), compute assembly with the brief's kind and write RUN_DIR/assembly.jsonl lines {id, kind, assembly}. Rows with ok false get {id, kind, assembly: null}. It never modifies validation.jsonl. Print `assembled X of Y valid`.

Add tests: a temp RUN_DIR with a validation.jsonl and GLBs made by makeGlb (one assembled static, one scattered static, one set with 3 separate grounded pieces, one ok:false row); assert assembly.jsonl contents and the printed summary. Extend tests/js/validate_glb.test.mjs to assert stats.glb.assembly exists on an exported fixture page and that reasons are unchanged versus tests/fixtures/glb_raw/scene_mode_expected.jsonl behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: glb_assembly.mjs writes assembly.jsonl with the asserted values, never touches validation.jsonl (file hash unchanged in the test), and prints `assembled X of Y valid`
A GLB-mode validator run on the existing fixtures gives the same ok/reasons as before and adds stats.glb.assembly
docs/14 section 4 names the CLI and its flags exactly as implemented
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

steps: Create scripts/glb_repair.py exactly per docs/14 section 5: selection rules, message list, fix message text, sampling from the model row, outputs under RUN_DIR/repair/, resumable, `repaired X of Y`, summary.json {selected, attempted, repaired, ids_repaired, model, system_file, system_sha256}.

userStories.title: Seeds and best-of-N picker (teacher_generate, glb_bench, glb_best_of.py)
userStories.description: As a product user, I want several sampled candidates per brief and an automatic pick of the best one, using only automatic signals (docs/14 section 6).
steps: teacher_generate.py: add `--seed N`; on the Ollama native route set options.seed; record `seed` in each raw row only when given. Without --seed the request body and row are unchanged (assert in tests).

glb_bench.py: add `--seed N` (forwarded to teacher_generate) and `--run-suffix S` (run directory `<out-root>/<name><S>`). Without them the commands are identical to today (assert with --dry-run output).

Create scripts/glb_best_of.py per docs/14 section 6: inputs `--runs DIR [DIR ...] --briefs FILE --out DIR`; ranking keys in the given order using validation.jsonl and assembly.jsonl (compute assembly via `node scripts/glb_assembly.mjs` when a run lacks assembly.jsonl, or fail with a clear message if --no-compute); copy raw/<id>.json, the GLB, screenshots and the validation row of the winner into --out with `picked_from`; write --out/assembly.jsonl and --out/picks.json {id: {picked_from, rank_keys}}. Refuse --out under data/, out/ or eval/, and refuse when --out equals one of the inputs.

Tests (tests/py/test_glb_best_of.py) with three tiny fake run dirs: a brief valid only in run 3 picks run 3; two valid candidates where only one is assembled picks the assembled one; ties pick the first run; output dir passes the files glb_report.py needs (build_report runs on it).

userStories.title: Phase 2 data from ccore's set with an eval-leak guard (ccore_prep.py)
userStories.description: As the trainer, I want a clean prompt/completion dataset from ccore's validated examples, with eval subjects removed, ready for scripts/mesh_lora_hf.py (docs/14 section 7).
steps: Create scripts/ccore_prep.py per docs/14 section 7: read *.parquet in --parquet-dir with pandas/pyarrow (already in .venv; import inside main so pytest can import the module), map train-*.parquet to train.jsonl and validation-*.parquet to val.jsonl, build rows {id, domain, title, prompt:[{role:'system',content},{role:'user',content}], completion:[{role:'assistant',content}]}, drop reasoning_content, apply the 4 drop rules in order and count each, apply the leak list from --leak-file to the title only with whole-word case-insensitive matching (multi-word phrases match as phrases).

Support `--system ccore` (prompts/ccore_glb_system.txt, read-only) or a file path; record system_file and system_sha256 in stats.json. Support `--extra-run DIR` (repeatable) with `--extra-system FILE`: add rows from DIR/raw whose validation row is ok and whose assembly.jsonl entry is assembled; refuse any id present in bench/glb/briefs.jsonl.

Write DIR/stats.json: inputs with sha256, kept and dropped counts per reason per split, kept by domain, completion chars median and max, max_chars, leak_file sha256. Refuse --out under data/, out/ or eval/.

userStories.title: Operator wrapper for the imp jobs (imp_ops.sh)
userStories.description: As the operator agent in imp-ops, I want start/wait/status commands for the long local jobs, with the v3 prompt hash enforced, so the ops PRD never runs raw long commands.
steps: Create scripts/imp_ops.sh modelled on scripts/glb_ops.sh (same pid/exit/log files under runs/imp/jobs, same 540 s wait cap, same one-job-at-a-time rule): subcommands `preflight`, `start JOB`, `wait JOB`, `status`. Jobs: `v3s2` and `v3s3` run `.venv/bin/python scripts/glb_bench.py --out-root runs/glb_v3 --only glimmer-v3 --seed 2|3 --run-suffix -s2|-s3`; `repair-v3` runs `.venv/bin/python scripts/glb_repair.py --run runs/glb_v3/glimmer-v3 --model-row glimmer-v3`.

`start` refuses unless runs/glb_v3/PROMPT_FROZEN.json exists and its sha256 equals the sha256 of prompts/system_glb_v3.txt; print REFUSED with the reason. preflight prints Ollama up/down (curl localhost:11434/api/tags), the running job if any, the hash check, and `python3 ralph/build_prds.py --status | grep imp-1`.

RUNS root and the bench command are overridable by env vars (IMP_OPS_RUNS, IMP_OPS_BENCH) so tests can use a temp dir and a fake command. Tests (tests/py/test_imp_ops.py) run the script with a fake bench that sleeps 1 s and writes files: start/wait/status flow, refusal on a wrong hash, refusal of a second job while one runs, unknown job name.
acceptanceCriteria: start refuses when the frozen hash does not match prompts/system_glb_v3.txt and when another job is alive (both asserted)
wait returns within the cap and reports the job's exit code from the .exit file (asserted with the fake bench)
The real job commands printed by `IMP_OPS_DRY=1 scripts/imp_ops.sh start v3s2` match the commands in this story exactly (asserted)

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Ralph builds and tests tools with tiny fixtures, GLB files built inside the tests, fake HTTP servers on localhost and tiny parquet files written by the tests. It never calls the real Ollama, never runs the benchmark, never reads or writes runs/ and never writes under data/, out/ or eval/. Existing behaviour must not change when the new flags are absent: the default scene mode of validate_scenes.mjs, GLB-mode failure reasons, teacher_generate.py rows without --seed, glb_bench.py run directory names without --run-suffix, and the existing glb_report.py columns. Do not edit bench/glb/briefs.jsonl, bench/glb/dev_briefs.jsonl, bench/glb/eval_subjects.json or any file in prompts/.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.

universal: `bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
